Situation1: It seems your friend is confused about the meeting spot, and you need to send a message right now to confirm it.
Situation2: Two travelers with several suitcases ask for help loading and plan to split the fare
Story:
I glanced at my phone, heart pounding. My friend’s last message was a jumble of questions about where we were supposed to meet tonight. I could sense the confusion, and I knew if I didn’t clear things up now, we’d probably miss each other entirely. But just as I started typing a reply, two travelers approached my cab, dragging heavy suitcases behind them. “Can you help us load these? We want to split the fare,” one of them asked, already opening the trunk. 

As a taxi driver, I’m supposed to be attentive, professional, and quick to help. I could see their impatience, and I knew I needed to focus on them—help with the bags, make sure the meter was set, and get them on their way. But my friend was waiting for an answer, probably getting more anxious by the minute. My phone buzzed again in my pocket. I felt torn, caught between being the reliable friend who communicates and the professional driver who puts customers first. My hands hovered, unsure whether to reach for the suitcases or my phone.
